intuition: A node must obey every ancestor's rule, not only its parent's rule. Carry a lower and upper allowed value as you visit the tree. Moving left lowers the upper limit; moving right raises the lower limit. Reject any node outside its allowed range.

Associate each pending node with an open numeric interval. The interval summarizes every ancestor constraint without retaining all ancestor values separately. For a left child, the parent becomes a stricter upper bound; for a right child, it becomes a stricter lower bound. Infinite initial endpoints admit any legal integer at the root.
The explicit stack gives the same depth-first reasoning as recursion while avoiding the interpreter’s recursion-depth limit on a long chain.

Each stack entry records exactly the bounds imposed by its ancestors. Passing those bounds means the node is correctly placed relative to all ancestors. The children receive the additional constraint from their parent. Therefore every node passes if and only if the whole tree obeys the strict subtree property.
The depth-first stack contains pending branches bounded by tree height h; worst-case h=n.

concept.question: Why must a node obey all ancestor bounds, rather than just its parent?
intuition: A child may look correct beside its parent yet violate a more distant ancestor’s ordering rule. Checking only adjacent values misses that inherited restriction.
Carry an allowed open interval down the tree. A left child inherits a smaller upper limit, while a right child inherits a larger lower limit. A node must fall strictly between every inherited bound.
concept.observation: The allowed interval is strict and contains all ancestor restrictions.
approach: Visit a node with its inherited lower and upper bounds.
Reject a value outside those strict bounds.
Pass narrowed bounds to the children.
concept.correctness: The root has unrestricted bounds. Each child receives the intersection of inherited ancestor bounds with its parent’s new restriction. If every node passes, every left-subtree value is smaller and every right-subtree value is larger than each ancestor it depends on. Conversely, any violated search-tree rule produces a failed inherited bound.

complexity.explanation: Visit each node once. The iterative depth-first frontier uses memory proportional to tree height in the worst case.
